title: Candles
hook: a candle as a prayer that keeps burning when you leave

segments.voice: Yesterday, incense: smoke that rises the way a prayer hopes to. Your line was prayer rises. When you saw steam or smoke climbing yesterday, what did you send up with it? Day one thousand three hundred sixty-one.

Near the side wall of a church, a stand of small candles. Some are burning. Some have burned down to a puddle of wax. Some are new, waiting. A man comes in on his lunch break, still in his work jacket. He drops a coin in the box, takes a fresh candle, lights it from one already burning, and sets it in its place. He stands for a moment. Then he checks the time and goes back out into the noise. The candle doesn't go with him. It keeps burning in the quiet church, for whoever he lit it for, long after he's back at his desk. Today: candles.

For the people who light one, a candle in church does something a spoken prayer can't: it keeps going when they stop. Start with light itself. "Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path." In the psalm, light is what lets you take the next step. And Jesus says a light is meant to be seen: "Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it giveth light unto all that are in the house." A candle on a stand is that sentence, burning. Next, a fire that stays lit. In Leviticus, the priests are told: "The fire shall ever be burning upon the altar; it shall never go out." Then, prayer that doesn't stop. Paul tells the church in Thessalonica, "Pray without ceasing." Nobody can talk without ceasing. So some Christians, Orthodox and Catholic among them, light a candle before an icon or a statue, for someone who is sick, someone far away, someone who has died, and say that the flame goes on praying after they've walked out the door. Other churches light candles in their own ways, on an Advent wreath or held in the hand on Christmas Eve. And last, the person. Proverbs goes further: "The spirit of man is the candle of the LORD." In that picture, a candle isn't only something a person lights. A person is one. So the small flame on the stand is lit by someone, for someone. A prayer left burning.
screen: `THE SPIRIT OF MAN IS THE CANDLE OF THE LORD.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: light a candle for someone. If you have one and it's safe, light it now and set it where you can see it. If not, turn on a small lamp, or simply look at any light near you. Settle, and breathe. Bring one person to mind, someone you love, someone struggling, someone you miss. Let the flame stand for them. If you pray, you can hold them in your prayer while you watch it. If you don't, simply keep them in mind, as steady as the flame. When the bell comes, you can leave the candle burning while you stay nearby. The bell holds the time.
Candles. Small flames lit in churches for someone, living or dead, so a prayer can go on burning after the person who lit it has gone.
Your line: a prayer left burning. Today, leave one small light on for someone, a porch light, a lamp in a window, a text that says you're thinking of them. Day one thousand three hundred sixty-one.

howItsDone: In Orthodox and Catholic churches people light small candles before icons and statues for the living and the dead and leave them burning; other churches light candles on an Advent wreath or hold them at candlelight services.

pairs: the fire shall never go out

myth: people light candles in some churches and leave them burning after they go
the flame stands for someone, and goes on after the person who lit it has gone.
Jesus says a lit candle belongs under a bushel
the opposite: "on a candlestick; and it giveth light unto all that are in the house."

fork.setup: on your lunch break you've lit a candle in a quiet church for someone you love. it's time to go back to work. what do you do with the candle?
options: blow it out before you leave
stay until it burns all the way down
fork.reveal: people leave it burning: a prayer that goes on after they've walked out the door.

original.note: Greek: lamp, the word the King James renders "candle" in Matthew 5:15.

trapdoor: what you thought: lighting a candle in church is just a nice gesture.
what it means: a small prayer for someone, which keeps burning after you've left.
what a scholar hears: Proverbs 20:27, "The spirit of man is the candle of the LORD": in the Bible, a person can be the candle.

notes: 'Some Christians... say that the flame goes on praying after they've walked out the door' is attributed, not asserted; confirm Catholic and Orthodox Keepers are comfortable with it.
'Somebody had to tend it, all night, every night' is inference from Leviticus 6:12–13; confirm or cut.
Greek lychnos in Matthew 5:15 rendered 'candle' in the KJV; confirm.
Advent wreath and Christmas Eve candles mentioned as other churches' customs, unquantified.
Practice includes a safety condition for lighting a candle; a lamp is offered instead.

Editor: cut the inferred 'all night, every night' tending claim; removed a repeated sentence about Orthodox and Catholic candles; 'young church' (an age claim) now names Thessalonica; replaced stock 'striking line'; the Proverbs image no longer tells the listener what they are; fixed 'stand stands'.
Audit (2026-10-02): opening claim about what a candle does is now attributed to the people who light them, not asserted by the narrator.
